title: Neighbor notes: First qualifying slip
summary: Produce readings[i] - readings[i-1] for i from 1 onward, preserving that order. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.
descriptionMd:
Two adjacent gauge readings describe how the press changed between successive sheets. Alma needs the first qualifying slip while the courier waits at the door. Later matches must not jump ahead in the tray.

Produce readings[i] - readings[i-1] for i from 1 onward, preserving that order.

Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.

Implement neighborNotesFirstQualifyingSlip(readings, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: Adjacent array positions. Produce readings[i] - readings[i-1] for i from 1 onward, preserving that order. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys (earlier units are used while the first two levels establish the foundations).
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with adjacent array positions. What state describes the portion you have already processed?
Produce readings[i] - readings[i-1] for i from 1 onward, preserving that order. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [-10,10,-7,12]. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. This gives 10.
The derived sequence is [0,-6,6]. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. This gives 6.
The derived sequence is []. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. This gives -1.
